verses.text: Now concerning the [things] sacrificed to idols, we know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.

verses.text: If anyone thinks to know anything, he does not yet know as it is necessary to know.

segments.text: If anyone thinks to know anything, he does not yet know as it is necessary to know.

verses.text: But if anyone loves God, he is known by Him.

verses.text: Therefore concerning the eating of the [things] sacrificed to idols, we know that an idol [is] nothing in [the] world and that [there is] no God except one.

verses.text: For even if indeed there are [those] called gods, whether in heaven or on earth—just as there are many gods and many lords—

verses.text: yet to us [there is] one God, the Father, of whom [are] all things, and we for Him; and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom [are] all things, and we through Him.

verses.text: But the knowledge [is] not in all. And some, by the habit of the idol until now, eat [such] as a thing sacrificed to an idol; and their conscience being weak, it is defiled.

verses.text: But food will not commend us to God; neither if we should eat do we fall short, nor if we should not eat do we excel.

verses.text: But take care, lest somehow this authority of yours⁺ become a stumbling block to the weak.

verses.text: For if anyone should see you, the [one] having knowledge, reclining in an idol’s temple, will not the conscience of him being weak be built up to eat the [things] sacrificed to idols?

verses.text: For the [one] being weak is destroyed by your knowledge—the brother for whom Christ died.

verses.text: And thus sinning against the brothers and wounding their conscience—[it] being weak—you⁺ sin against Christ.

verses.text: Therefore, if food causes my brother to stumble, never shall I eat meat to the age, so that I shall not cause my brother to stumble.
